title: Evolutionary Compatibility Playbook: behavior flags, migration guides, and regression tests for streaming, tool-calls, and structured outputs
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description: Goal: produce a prescriptive playbook and runnable artifacts for evolving Redwood's Core API surface (streaming, function/tool calling, structured outputs) while preserving customer integrations. The deliverables are: 1) a set of behavior flags and default semantics per API minor version, 2) migration guides for customers and SDKs, 3) a regression/baseline test harness for backward compatibility, and 4) a staged deprecation schedule with canary rollout and automatic fallback behavior. This ticket coordinates PM, Eng, and DX and captures decisions, risks, and a rollout checklist.
behavior_flags: tool_calling: enum {legacy_inline, explicit_tools_v1, tools_v2} (controls whether model emits function call tokens or structured tool objects)
compat_fallback: boolean (runtime policy to auto-fallback to compatible model/variant)
compat_strictness: enum {lenient, strict} (how strictly we validate older clients against new responses)
migration_steps: Audit existing public API behaviors and all SDK surface tests that assume legacy streaming framing
Define mapping table: legacy behavior -> behavior_flag settings & recommended customer changes
Draft SDK changes and feature flags in SDKs (python/js/go) with opt-in toggles
Author migration guides: minimal changes, sample diffs for typical use-cases (chat, tool-call, structured outputs), and example error handling
Create compatibility test vectors (seed prompts + expected token sequences + structured output snapshots)
Run internal migration on 2 non-production tenants and collect telemetry (latency, error delta, format diffs)
Publish staged deprecation notice and timeline to Console and email admins
Perform canary rollout with 1% traffic to new default behavior and monitor for regressions
deprecation_schedule: 2026-05-01: Announce deprecation window for legacy streaming framing and legacy inline tool-calls
2026-06-01: SDKs release opt-in flags defaulting to legacy (no user impact)
2026-08-01: New minor API (vX.Y+1) defaults to new behavior_flag settings; legacy remains behind explicit flag
2026-11-01: Legacy behavior enters best-effort support (>=90-day final removal countdown), with console warnings on affected routes
2027-02-01: Legacy behavior removed from hosted default runtime; private deployments receive upgrade guide
backward_compatibility_tests: Golden token stream comparisons for 200 representative chat prompts (legacy vs new framing)
Function-call roundtrip tests: model emits function call -> SDK parses -> runtime invokes mock tool -> model continues
Structured output schema validation across json_schema_v1 and typed_schema_v2
End-to-end customer fixture tests for 10 highest-traffic customers (anonymized fixtures)
Stress tests under batching/kv-cache scenarios to detect timing-dependent regressions
Fuzzing harness for incremental parser changes (stream reassembly edge cases)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Internal): unit + integration tests, feature-flag QA in staging (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (Canary): 1% hosted traffic + selected beta customers opt-in (4 weeks)
Phase 2 (Gradual): 10%, 25%, 50% checks with automated rollback triggers on error budget burn or >0.5% format-delta in top-10 routes
Phase 3 (Default Flip): switch default for new minor release; provide 30-day escape hatch flag for customers
Phase 4 (Removal): after 90-day final notice, remove legacy code-path and mark deprecation complete
risks: Undetected parser edge-cases in streaming framing that break long-lived client connections
Tool-calling semantics mismatch causing silent mis-invocations in production SDK integrations
Customers with bespoke parsing (regex-based) will break without clear diffs / examples
Latency regressions when enabling stricter validation or new framing protocol
Private deployments may be slow to apply upgrades, requiring extended support window
decisions: Default policy: new minor API releases may change default behavior flags but not remove legacy behavior until explicit removal window
Expose behavior_flags in runtime API and SDKs to allow per-route overrides
Provide automated migration CLI and SDK helpers to translate legacy client flows to new formats
Require signal-based rollout (canary metrics + automated rollback) for changes that affect streaming framing or tool-calling defaults
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility harness green on baseline regression suite for full staging cluster
Migration guide reviewed and sign-off from DX, Eng, and Legal for data-handling language
SDKs (python/js/go) support opt-in behavior_flags and pass the SDK integration test matrix
Observability: dashboards track format-delta, parser-errors, latency percentiles, and customer-affected routes
Runbook and rollback steps validated in a simulated incident run
